output.summary: Perennial mustard-family plant native to southern Europe, Mediterranean countries and Asia east to the Himalayas. It has waxy leaves, small white flowers and an extensive deep root network. Its leaves, shoots and fruits are edible; in Ladakh, young growth is boiled and soaked to remove bitterness before being cooked like spinach.
output.edibilityNote: Leaves, shoots and fruits are edible; in Ladakh, young growth is boiled, soaked for two days and cooked like spinach.
